Around that time, I got really fixated on sex—hookup apps, risky stuff I normally wouldn’t do. I even put a bunch of money, like most of my savings, into this sketchy delivery “startup idea” with some guy I barely know, without really reading anything.

I’ve also had moments where I’m sure this girl I’ve been seeing is cheating on me, even though I don’t really have proof. Sometimes I see people in my apartment or on the street—just standing there or moving past me—and then they’re gone when I look twice.

Before all that, and again more recently, I’ve had months where I just feel low, empty. Things I used to enjoy—music on the road, hanging out—don’t feel like anything. D010-D006_h001.question_a:
It kind of feels like my whole life’s been split in two this past year.  

About seven months ago I hit this…high. For like two months straight I barely slept and didn’t even feel tired. I was always on the move—doing extra delivery shifts, then coming home and pacing or going for long drives at 2 a.m. My mood was all over the place; one minute I’d be on top of the world, joking, laughing, and the next I’d snap at people over nothing. My coworkers couldn’t keep up with how fast I was talking—I’d jump from one topic to another and it felt physically uncomfortable to shut up.  

I got super focused on sex too—hookup apps nonstop, risky stuff I wouldn’t usually do. I even put a bunch of money I don’t really have into this sketchy “delivery startup” some guy on Discord pitched me, didn’t really read anything, just wired it.  

During that time I also became convinced my ex was cheating on me, even though we weren’t even together. I kept “seeing” guys standing near her car or outside my apartment—full-on people, then they’d just vanish. That only happened during that high phase.  

Then I crashed. For the last five months I’ve just felt flat and low. I don’t enjoy anything—music, games, even driving feels pointless. I can’t decide on simple stuff like what to eat, so I just skip meals. I’m calling in sick, missing shifts. I’m not seeing things or having those cheating thoughts anymore, just this heavy, empty feeling that won’t lift.
D010-D006_h001.question_b:
I drive for a courier company, so my days are usually long, but for about two months recently I was like a motor that wouldn’t shut off. I barely slept and still felt wired, pacing, taking extra routes just to keep moving. I’d go from feeling on top of the world to snapping at coworkers or customers over nothing in the same hour. I couldn’t stop talking, even when people looked uncomfortable—I’d ramble, jump from topic to topic, and silence felt unbearable. My sex drive went through the roof; I was messaging multiple women, including exes, and pushing for hookups constantly. I even tried to start this “side logistics company,” threw a bunch of my savings into some sketchy app and trucks I hadn’t really researched.

During that time I was sure my ex was cheating on me, checking her socials nonstop, convinced every comment was proof, even though we weren’t together. I also saw people in the back of my van or on the street who disappeared when I looked twice.

Then I crashed. For about five months I’ve mostly felt flat and low, like nothing is enjoyable anymore—not friends, games, sex, anything. Getting dressed or choosing what to eat can paralyze me. I’m messing up routes and sometimes can’t even leave my bed. But even in these really down weeks, when I’m not amped up at all, I still sometimes see figures in my apartment or in my mirrors and get stuck on the idea that my ex is secretly with someone else, even though I know it doesn’t make sense.

Around that time I became convinced something was wrong inside my body—like my organs were decaying, even though all my tests were normal. I’d also get these strange, metallic or chemical tastes out of nowhere, like I’d swallowed lab reagents.

After that, I crashed. For the last five months I’ve felt really low and flat, mostly staying in our apartment, avoiding friends and even family calls. Work has been a mess; I stare at code and can’t keep a clear line of thought, like my brain is under water. Even answering simple emails feels overwhelming. My husband says I’m not myself at all.

I couldn’t sit still in meetings; I’d pace, jump from one idea to the next, talking nonstop so my team could barely get a word in. I was convinced every article, podcast, even random comments in the office had some special message just for me, about my business or my “destiny.” 

I also kept getting these odd tastes, like metal or something sweet and chemical in my mouth, out of nowhere. Around that same time my sex drive went through the roof. I started flirting with employees, and I had a couple of affairs on business trips that are completely out of character for me and have really shaken my marriage and the company.

Then I crashed. For the last five months I’ve felt hollow, like someone turned the color off. I don’t care about golf, or the company, or much of anything. I’m forgetting simple things—where I put my keys, what I was about to say—and it’s embarrassing in front of my staff. The strange “messages” and tastes stopped once that high period ended; now it’s just this heavy emptiness and going through the motions.
D010-D006_h005.question_b:
For about seven months now I’ve felt like I’ve been living in two completely different gears.

The first stretch, maybe two months, I was on fire. I barely slept, maybe three hours a night, but I didn’t feel tired. I’d be pacing the house, hopping between emails, new product ideas, reorganizing the whole company structure at 3 a.m. I couldn’t sit still in meetings; I’d talk nonstop, cutting people off, jumping from one idea to the next. I felt on top of the world, like everything was clicking. I also got very sexually driven—porn constantly, flirting with employees, and I actually hooked up with a junior staffer on a business trip, which is completely unlike me and has really damaged my marriage and the company.

During that “high,” I became convinced TV anchors were sending me signals about our business strategy, and sometimes water or coffee would suddenly taste like metal or chemicals, even when others said it was normal.

Then that high just disappeared. For the last five months I’ve felt hollow, like there’s nothing inside. I’ve lost interest in golf, seeing friends, even the business. I can’t focus; I misplace documents, forget appointments. Work has really suffered. But even in this flat, empty state, I still sometimes feel the news is aimed directly at me, and I still get those strange, phantom tastes, even though the “up” mood is completely gone.

When I talk, it’s like my mouth runs ahead of my head. My wife keeps telling me to slow down because she can’t follow what I’m saying, and I get mad when she cuts in. I’ve also been doing…stupid things. I’ve gone into town and flirted and fooled around with women I barely know. That’s not something I ever used to do, and I know it’s hurting my marriage and our reputation.

Lately I’m convinced my wife is sneaking around on me. I watch her phone, her comings and goings, certain she’s hiding something, even though I can’t really prove anything. It’s hard to explain without jumping around a bit. For the last seven months or so, I’ve mostly felt…flat and worn out. I go to the library because I have to, but I move like I’m underwater. I just don’t care about things the way I used to—programs, cataloging projects, even reading. I come home and lie on the couch. I sleep enough hours, but I wake up feeling like I barely slept. Most mornings I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans or anything like that.

There was this stretch about three weeks long, maybe a couple of months ago, where everything flipped. I was snapping at patrons over small things, pacing the stacks, rearranging sections in the middle of the night in my head. I couldn’t stop talking in staff meetings—I’d leap from one idea to another and get irritated when people didn’t keep up. I had way more energy than usual but it actually made work harder; I couldn’t focus.

Around that time—and a bit outside of it too—I started feeling like comments on the radio or people whispering in the reading room were somehow about me. And sometimes I catch this strange, burnt, almost chemical smell that no one else seems to notice, even when I ask.
D010-D006_h018.question_a:

I’ve been dragging myself to the library, but once I’m there I just stare at the circulation desk or the catalog screen and can’t make myself do anything. I used to love planning displays and talking to patrons; now I mostly hope no one needs me. I wake up exhausted no matter how early I go to bed, like sleep doesn’t “take.” A lot of nights I lie there thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up, not planning anything, just wishing I could be done.

Then, about three weeks ago, it flipped. I suddenly had so much energy I was pacing the stacks, rearranging shelves at 2 a.m., barely sleeping and not feeling tired. I’ve been snapping at coworkers and patrons over tiny things. I can’t stop talking in meetings; my mind races faster than I can get the words out. Around the same time, I started feeling like patrons’ whispers and even book titles were sending me special messages, and I kept smelling smoke in the building when no one else did. D010-D006_h018.question_b:

I’d go to the library and just sit at the desk staring at the catalog system, unable to make myself shelve books or answer emails. I was constantly down, like there was a weight on my chest. Even when I slept 8–9 hours, I’d wake up feeling as if I hadn’t rested at all. I’d catch myself thinking, “It would be easier if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow,” though I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.

Then about three weeks ago, it flipped. I got this surge of energy, couldn’t sit still at the reference desk, pacing the stacks, talking nonstop to coworkers and patrons until they looked uncomfortable. Little things set me off; if someone whispered too loudly, I’d snap at them. I barely needed sleep and still felt wired.

All through this—during the low months, and even in the two weeks before I “sped up”—I’ve been convinced that comments on the radio and patrons’ conversations are secretly about me. I also keep smelling smoke in the library and in my apartment, like something’s burning, but no one else smells it and there’s nothing there.

A few times I’ve even seen someone standing in our hallway or at the foot of the bed, like a clear figure, but when I look again they’re not there. I can’t tell if it’s just my head playing tricks on me or something worse, and it’s making it really hard to function at home and at school.

I’ve been having awful, vivid nightmares almost every night, and I wake up drenched in sweat. On the worst days, when I’m crossing a street or standing on the balcony at school, I get these sudden urges to just step out into traffic or over the railing. I’ve never made a plan, but the impulse scares me. It’s made it really hard to keep up at work and at home with my husband.

I barely sleep but don’t feel tired; I’m buzzing all day, pacing around, reorganizing my classroom at 3 a.m., texting parents long messages full of “great ideas.” My husband says I talk without breathing, jumping from one topic to another, and I get annoyed if anyone tries to slow me down. At school, I can’t stick to the schedule; I keep starting big projects with the kids and ignoring the lesson plans.

Around the same time this “high” started, I became totally convinced my husband is cheating, even though there’s nothing concrete—just him checking his phone or staying a bit late at work. It feels absolutely certain in my head. I’ve also started seeing things that no one else sees: shadows moving in the hallway, strange figures at the edge of my vision, sometimes a man standing in our bedroom doorway who disappears when I blink. At the factory, I move like I’m underwater. The guys on my line complain I’m too slow picking parts up, and I can feel my body just not wanting to move faster. When I’m walking home after night shift, it’s like my legs are full of sand. In that time I’ve thought a lot about just ending it, down to where I’d do it and how, picturing it pretty clearly. That scares me, but it also feels…weirdly calm.

Before this low part, there was about two weeks where I was the complete opposite. I was snapping at everyone over nothing, like any small thing set me off. I had so much energy I couldn’t sit still, pacing through the break room, starting three jobs at once and finishing none because my mind kept jumping around.

On and off through all of this, I get these ideas that my ex is sneaking around with someone else, even though we’re not really together and I don’t have proof. I check his socials, drive past his place after work. Sometimes at night, on the walk home, I see people standing by the road, or a shadow moving that looks like a person—but when I get closer, there’s no one there. I can’t always tell if it’s just me being tired from night shifts or something else, but it feels very real in the moment.
